MD&A itself warns that further tariffs could cut sales.

In this case energy, supply and tariff costs catch up with pricing, and change orders fail to recover them. Restructuring and transformation costs keep recurring. The one-off AFFF recoveries and the divestiture gain disappear. The margin sits just above continuing pretax income as a share of revenue, with little credit for adding back the interest charge.
operating_margin_year_one.quote: The ongoing conflicts in the Middle East have disrupted energy supplies and supply chains, increased costs for energy and other supplies and created volatility in the capital markets, among other impacts.

Capital spending, now below depreciation and amortization, has to come back up. Each unit of growth therefore takes more of after-tax operating income.

revenue_growth_year_one.reason: Management raised its full-year organic sales outlook. Orders rose on large projects and data centers, and Americas backlog grew. Reported revenue will grow more slowly than organic sales, though: ADT Spain and ADT Mexico are sold, ADT United Kingdom is held for sale, and the orders growth is measured on a wider definition than the prior orders it is compared with. So the base sits below the guided organic rate and the latest quarter's pace, close to trailing four-quarter growth.

The order book justifies the step up from the three-year record. The gap to the latest quarter allows for divestitures and for the changed orders definition.

terminal_growth.reason: A mature building-systems and services business should grow with nominal output in the long run. The services base and data-center demand keep it there, not above it. The risk-free rate caps it.

operating_margin_year_one.reason: The record has no operating-income row, so the margin is built from what is filed. Continuing pretax income, which is after interest expense, sets a floor. The base adds back the interest charge that the record does not carry. It removes the AFFF insurance recoveries and the ADT Mexico gain, which MD&A says lowered SG&A this year and which will not repeat. It keeps restructuring and transformation costs in, because they recur every period. Gross margin is at its record and pricing is offsetting cost pressure, so the starting point does not assume erosion.

operating_margin_year_ten.reason: Management guides operating leverage, the share of added sales that reaches profit, well above the current margin. So the margin should widen as revenue grows. But the guidance has just become a range with a low end below the old figure, restructuring recurs, and incentive and corporate costs are rising. The base therefore takes a gradual widening, not the full guided leverage.

The record shows the margin widening, and the year-ten margin continues that path at a slower pace. There is no filed operating margin to check it against.

reinvestment_rate_year_one.reason: Capital expenditure is below depreciation and amortization. Much of that gap is amortization of acquired intangibles, so capital spending only roughly maintains the asset base and cannot stay below depreciation for long. Growth draws on working capital: receivables rose faster than revenue, partly offset by deferred revenue and payables. It also draws on bolt-on acquisitions such as Alloy and Nantum. The base reinvests more than the trailing net figure, so the order book is funded.
